counterfactual_missing_items: Ascitic fluid polymorphonuclear count >250/μL to confirm SBP
Explicit exposure history to raw seafood or wound
decisive_items: Blood culture positive with grayish white colonies on blood agar and green colonies on TCBS agar
A 53-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (>30 years)
response.rationale: C1 uniquely combines the confirmed Vibrio vulnificus bacteremia (TCBS green colonies, 16S rRNA) with the chronic HBV/cirrhosis predisposition, explaining the fever, lumbar pain, and ascites. R1 is a correlated subset lacking host context; R2 captures the lumbar complication but not the organism; R4 is below the SBP PMN threshold and ignores the blood culture; R3 is a nonspecific syndrome.

rejected.why: Correlated subset of C1; identifies Vibrio but omits the chronic HBV/cirrhosis risk factor, so less complete.
Ascites cell count 200/μL is below the SBP threshold and it ignores the blood culture and lumbar findings.
Sepsis is a nonspecific syndrome; the raw microbiology and host risk factors point to a specific Vibrio diagnosis.
